Commentary.Commentary: That brings us to the close of a one-sided affair. The visitors lacked in preparation and faltered in conditions where the ball was moving sideways. Their youngsters need to learn how to be patient and construct an innings. A lot of soul searching to do for them. On the other hand, the Kiwis have started off their home season with supreme confidence. Good all-round show was on display and they will be eager to carry that forward in the limited overs contest as well. Let us hope that the Windies play to their potential and put up a better fight. Join us for the 1st ODI from Whangarei on 20th December at 1100 local (2200 GMT, previous day). Till then, cheers!

New Zealand skipper, Kane Williamson says that they put together two strong performances on the board. Credits his players for the way they executed their plans. Feels that a target of 440-odd on the board was good enough as the wicket was getting variable. Reckons that both the teams fought hard. Adds there was little movement in the air and off the pitch. Feels that they are fortunate to be on the right side. Is happy that they are back in home conditions and doing well. Praises Taylor and says that it is a special moment for him as he equaled Martin Crowe's record of 17 Test tons. Opines that his century was very important in the context of the game.

Windies skipper, Kraigg Brathwaite congratulates New Zealand. Mentions they need to improve a lot as a side. Feels that his bowlers did a brilliant job. Adds that Roach was struggling a bit but everyone stood up. States that he enjoyed his first stint as a captain. Ends by saying that it is a tough loss and going forward they will want to rectify their mistakes.

Man of the Match, Ross Taylor says that the focus was on winning the game and he is happy with the team's performance. Adds that he feels sorry for Williamson as the skipper scored his tons (17) much quicker as compared to him. Mentions that he took confidence from his strokeplay in Wellington. Adds that he built upon that and it came out well. States that they wanted to win the series but the visitors put them under pressure on various occasions. Ends by saying that they stood together through tough times and are the deserved winners.

After gaining a handy lead of 152, the hosts did lose a couple of early wickets but it wasn't going to trouble them much. Williamson scored a free-flowing fifty while Ross Taylor hit a measured ton to take the home side to a formidable total. The visitors faltered in the run chase, gifting their wickets away with their reckless approach and were handed a big defeat. Be with us as the presentation is coming up...

The Windies in reply were not good enough. Apart from Brathwaite who scored a fifty, no one really applied themselves and were found wanting in testing conditions. Boult was in his elements picking up a 4-wicket haul while the other seamers grabbed two wickets each.

Earlier, New Zealand posted a good total on the board on the back of a resolute 84 from Jeet Raval, a breezy half century from Colin de Grandhomme and the 61-run last wicket stand between Trent Boult and Tim Southee. Shannon Gabriel was the pick of the bowlers for the visitors, taking a 4-fer but gave away too many no balls - 7 to be precise.

The 78-run stand between Chase and Reifer did give the tourists something to feel good about though. The former scored a classy fifty while the latter showed good resilience but they eventually crumbled under the tall ask.

Another emphatic show from the Black Caps and they take the series 2-0. The Windies were caught in a hole even before this day started. Not much resistance from them and they kept on sloping downhill. The visitors had their hopes pinned on the pair of Brathwaite and Hope but both of them disappointed.

OUT! Bowled 'em! That's the final nail in the coffin. A thoroughly comprehensive victory for the Kiwis. Santner pushes this one quicker through the air on middle and off, Roach plays for the turn which is not present and he ends up being beaten completely, to hear the noise of timber. Santner is pumped and his teammates are ecstatic. Customary handshakes all around. NEW ZEALAND WIN BY 240 RUNS AND TAKE THE SERIES 2-0!
Shannon Gabriel is the last man in.

OUT! Cummins holes out! Tossed up delivery around off, Cummins looks to heave it over mid on but the ball skews off the outer half of his bat over mid off. Boult backtracks from the same region and takes a good catch.
Sits deep in the crease and blocks it watchfully.
Uppish but safe! Cummins goes for a big slog but gets a top edge. The ball skies towards long on. The fielder from mid off backtracks but the ball falls down safely.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. One run added to the total.
Change in bowling. Mitchell Santner to roll his arm over now.

SIX! What a shot! Cummins get into the act as well. Full delivery on off, Cummins clears his front leg and tonks it over deep mid-wicket for a biggie. 200 up for the Windies, something to smile about for them.

Roach is lucky! Yorker around off, Roach tries to dig it out but seems to have missed it as the ball carries to the keeper. The hosts appeal but the umpire stays put. Hot Spot shows that the ball brushed the toe-end of the bat before the bat hit the ground.
Goes for a slog but misses.
The ball is way wide on the leg side but the batsman still goes after it.

In the air... but safe! Backs away to the short ball and top edges his heave just over the man at mid-wicket. A run taken. Roach calls his partner through for the second and his partner is late to respond. However, he makes it to the non-striker's end just in time.
SIX! Going, going, gone! Roach backs away to the short ball and murders it over cow corner for a maximum.
The session is getting extended. Usually it happens when a sole wicket is remaining but the umpires have stretched it. Don't know for how long. Not sure you can do it.
Tucks this one around the corner for a run.
FOUR! Roach is having fun. Gets a short ball in his arc and hammers it over mid on for another boundary.
The batsman works it down the leg side. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.
Ouch! Back of a length ball, Roach looks to heave it away but is hit on the stomach.
The batsman fails to put bat on ball.
FOUR! Smashed! Full ball outside off, Roach bludgeons it through covers and the ball rockets to the fence like a tracer bullet.
Last over before Tea if a wicket doesn't fall.
Down the leg side, Cummins looks to play it across but misses.
Bouncer outside off, comfortably evaded.
How will you explain that shot? Very full ball on leg stump, Roach aims to clip it but gets it off the toe-end of the bat to third man. A flick off the bottom edge to third man it is, outrageous.
That will sting! Shortish delivery on leg stump, Roach takes his eyes off the ball and is hit on the chest. Needs to be careful or he will end up injured.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Short ball down the leg side, Roach pulls it towards fine leg. The fielder moves to his left but the ball lands in front of him. A run taken.
Sits back and defends it with a straight bat.
Blocks the incoming delivery past short leg.
Prods forward to the moving delivery and keeps it out.
The batsman failed to make contact and was hit low on the pads.
Brilliant delivery. Full and fast outside off, Cummins pokes at it and misses.
Full delivery outside off, swinging away. Cummins has a play and a miss.
Hangs back to the full delivery and keeps it out.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

Not Out! No, there isn't any outside edge. Very full delivery leaving the right-hander. He aims to jam it out but seems to have missed it. Blundell dives full length to his right and takes it one-handed. Southee appeals but the umpire stays put. The keeper is not sure but Williamson goes for a review after a chat with the bowler. The Hot Spot doesn't spot anything. Even the Snicko shows no involvement of the bat. The on-field call is upheld. New Zealand lose a review but it does not matter in the context of the game. The sound was that of the bat hitting the ground.
Review time! Blundell has taken a terrific catch. Southee convinces his skipper to go for the review. Is there an outside edge?
The man at leg slip has gone deeper.
Another one outside leg, Roach goes for another big shot but only connects with thin air.
Back of a length delivery outside leg stump, Roach goes for another pull but misses.
FOUR! Nicely done! Southee runs in from around the wicket and bowls a short ball on leg stump. Roach expecting it swivels across and help pulls it through short fine leg to fine the ropes.
A leg slip and a short leg in place.
Outside off, Cummins has a feeble push at it but fails to make any contact.
The batsman failed to make contact and was hit low on the pads. One run added to the total. Leg bye signalled by the umpire.
Sharp bouncer on middle and leg, Kemar ducks under it in a flash.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Hangs back to the back of a length delivery and blocks it.
Length delivery angling across Roach who stays leg side of the ball and attempts to whack it through but gets beaten.
Outside off, Cummins pokes at it and gets beaten.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
In the zone outside off, left alone.
Fuller in length, kept out watchfully.
On a length on off, Cummins blocks it off the back foot.
Miguel Cummins strides out to bat.

OUT! One of the best catches that you will see in a game of cricket! However, the reaction was such that we felt that the ball had been grassed. On a drivable length outside off, Reifer prods forward and is drawn into the temptation. Pushes at it with hard hands and the ball flies towards gully. Williamson anticipates it really well, crouches to his left and seems to have grabbed a stunning one-handed catch. He stays down on the ground for a while. His teammates run towards him and it is then that the celebration begins. The replays confirm that he has taken it inches above the ground. A resolute knock from Reifer is cut short. New Zealand are two wickets away from a victory unless the retired hurt Sunil Ambris bats again.
Better from Roach! Good length ball on off, Kemar hangs back and defends it stoutly.
Another flashy shot to no use. Shaping away from Kemar as he attempts an agricultural shot through the off side but misses.
Almost drags it back! Length delivery angling across Roach. He tries to force it through covers but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
This one takes off from a good length around off, Reifer is surprised as he fends it towards covers while taking his bottom hand off. A run taken.
Beauty! Good length ball in the corridor of uncertainty, shaping away a touch after pitching. Reifer feels for it and is convincingly beaten.
Well bowled. On a drivable length outside off, the temptation is there to go for an ambitious drive but Reifer stays composed and lets it go.
Bumper on middle and leg, Kemar sits underneath it.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! Uppish but in fair control of that shot. Fractionally overpitched outside off, Roach leans a touch and drives it with an open face past the gully region for a boundary.
Dishes out a full length ball outside off, eased through covers for a run.
A short mid-wicket in place as Southee comes from around the wicket.
Angling into Roach who tries to tuck it away but misses. The ball brushes his thigh pad and rolls to short fine leg. A leg bye taken.
So close to the outside edge! Good length ball outside off, swinging away. Roach remains stranded in his crease and tries to drive it on the up but gets beaten.
A sharp short delivery, aiming at the body. Reifer ducks under it comfortably.
In the zone of apprehension, good bounce on it. Reifer points his bat upwards to allow it through.
Peach! On a length outside off, seaming away after hitting the deck. Raymon fishes at it half-heartedly and gets foxed.
Good length ball outside off, swinging away. Reifer keeps his bat inside the line and lets it go.
Back of a length ball around off, hits hard on the bat of Reifer who takes his top hand off after playing it beside him.
Full length ball on off, Reifer leans ahead and defends it solidly.
Trying to strangle Roach down the leg side. He moves inside the line, tries to glance it but misses.
Southee goes back to pounding the deck hard. Roach is nervy for a moment but does well to sit under it.
Good looking shot for no run! Fractionally overpitched outside off, caressed straight to the man at covers.
Back of a length ball on off, holding its line. Roach gets behind the line of the delivery and blocks it stoutly. That was a good defensive stroke from the tailender.
Another bouncer, this time on middle and leg, this time Kemar ducks under it in an awkward manner.
Southee bangs in a short ball on off, testing the tailender with a bouncer. He is alert and ducks under it in a jiffy.
Bouncer well outside off, Reifer drops his wrists and leaves it alone.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Places this one behind point for a run and gets off the mark.
Nervy! Back of a length ball, angling across Roach. He fishes at it and gets an outside edge towards gully.
Greets Roach with a short ball, he ducks under it.
Kemar Roach strides out to bat.

OUT! The bouncer brings in another reward. It is Wagner again who provides the needed breakthrough. He steams in and bangs in a well-directed short ball on leg stump, extracts appreciable zip as well. Chase goes for the big pull shot but miscues it towards deep backward square leg. Colin de Grandhomme moves to his left from long leg, keeps his eyes on the ball and takes it comfortably. The promising 78-run comes to an end. End is nigh for the visitors.

Is that a missed opportunity? Seems like it went on the full. Full length ball attacking the stumps, Reifer chips it to the left side of Southee who gets low and seems to have got his left hand to it but the ball bursts through. Rolls down to long on and a couple is taken.
Chase clips this one through backward square leg. While setting off for a run, he slips but manages to maintain his balance. He makes the other end safely.
Full length ball, eased towards mid off. Chase runs through to the other end and doesn't bother to ground his bat in. These little things can cost him.
Slower delivery on off, Reifer plays it with soft hands past the bowler towards mid off.
Similar delivery, placed nicely behind point for a run. Chase wants the second but the fielder is quick to attack the ball to deny the run.
Fullish delivery outside off, tapped with an open bat face to cover-point.

A wicketless hour for the Windies. That is actually well done. Predictions were there for the game to be over by this time but they have done well to keep New Zealand at bay. The Kiwis have tried everything and have bowled really well, drying out the runs, mixing up the lengths and also causing some frustration but have not been able to strike after the break. A bit of hammering going around the bowlers' landing area. They will believe that they are just a wicket away from causing a collapse and a quick finish. Meanwhile, the umpires pass the ball through the 8-shaped gauge but the shape of the ball is not good enough. A replacement has been called in. Tim Southee to have a go with it first up.
Four in a row! Comes around the wicket, bangs it in short again, RR ducks.
Third bouncer of the over, Raymon ducks once more.
Another bouncer, same reaction.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Just wide! A short ball around off, coming in, Reifer tucks it uppishly and gets it just past short leg. Replays show, however, that there was no bat involved.
WIDE. That has been banged right in the middle of the pitch, Reifer ducks. Umpire Oxenford signals a wide from square leg.
This was coming. A short ball, around off, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.
NEIL WAGNER is back on.

FOUR! Fine shot! Half volley outside off, Reifer leans and drives it through the covers for a boundary! 150 IS UP FOR WIN. The stand is worth 71 now. Interestingly, Raymon has moved to 24 and 20 of those have come in boundaries.
Outside off, Raymon pushes this to point and sets off for a single but is sent back.
Stays back in his crease this time and blocks once more.
De Grandhomme pulls out of his runup. Seems like he lost his rhythm.
Gets across his stumps and defends.
Outside off, quietly left alone.

A short ball on middle, Chase swivels and pulls it towards the fine leg fence. For a second, it seems like it will be another boundary but Neil Wagner quickly gets to the ball from long leg and keeps the batsmen to a single.

Good fielding effort from Santner. Chase drives it behind point and this time Mitchell Santner runs hard after it from point. He manages to get to the ball with a slide and pushes the ball back in just before it can touch the ropes. The third umpire confirms that a run has been saved. Chase moves to 60 with that. 11 from the over. Just kind of breaks the shackles.
FOUR! Second of the over! This is slightly short, around the hips and Chase just tucks it towards fine leg! The stand now moves to 63.
Around off, watchfully defended.
FOUR! 5TH TEST FIFTY for Chase! He is fighting hard. Keeping the Windies going. Full and wide outside off, Chase reaches out and drives it behind point for a boundary.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
A slip comes out and goes to short mid-wicket.
Excellent yorker on middle and well dug out too. Boult collects and has a shy at the striker's end but is pretty wide. Chase was out of his crease for a while.
Full and outside off, left alone.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

That is really very poor from Chase. Just when de Grandhomme is about to deliver, he just walks across to his left at the non-striker's end, that too, all of a sudden. Thankfully for the Windies, Reifer does not lose his focus and keeps this full ball towards cover.
FOUR! In the air but no one there. A length ball on middle and leg, Reifer flicks it uppishly through square leg and gets a boundary.
Full and outside off, swinging in, driven nicely towards mid off.
Flicks it away for a single.
On a length outside off, coming in, defended solidly. Dot ball to finish the over.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

50-RUN STAND IS UP! Something positive for the Windies. At 80/5, things looked done and dusted but this pair is at least trying to show some resistance. It is the last recognized batting stand and needs to be bigger than just 50. Flicks it through the leg side for a single.
On middle and leg, turned towards short mid-wicket.
Works this wide of mid on and takes a quick single.
On a length outside off, angling in, Reifer stays back and defends.

Mix-up, but safe! Things just about seem to be happening. Feels like something is going to give soon. New Zealand are stringing together plenty of dots and the pitch is starting to show some uneven bounce. The Windies are getting frustrated. Full and wide outside off, Chase leans and drives it through the covers. He thinks there is a single available and there might have been one, had Reifer taken off from the word go. But he was not that sure and sent Chase back who was halfway down the track. Luckily for the striker, Wagner had to cover a lot of ground from mid off and then slide to stop the ball, then throw.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
On middle and off, driven sweetly but mid on cuts it off.
Full and wide outside off, left alone.
Now he does play at that one, away from his body, without moving his feet and gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
That is well bowled. Full and outside off, enticing the drive and then making the ball swing away. However, Chase shoulders arms.
Outside off, confidently defended.
Outside off, pushed straight to cover.

Ahh.... effort ball from Boult. He keeps this very full and in line of the stumps, Reifer looks to defend but the ball just holds off the surface and lobs off the bat. Almost carries to the bowler. In the last couple of overs, we have seen some indifferent bounce. Is the pitch breaking up?
Flicks this away for a single.
Another leave outside off.
Wide outside off, left alone.
TRENT BOULT is back on. Looks like it will be the end of Santner for this game.
Full and on off, driven towards mid off.
Works this efficiently now for a single on the leg side.
Again. The length is full and Chase looks to drive but the ball hits the bat very high and he mistimes it a little.
Brings Chase forward and makes him tuck the ball. But it rises steeply and goes off the inner half, lobbing towards short mid-wicket.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.

Tea pots boiling? The umpires are having a chat with the batsmen and a couple of Kiwis are standing beside them. Looks like a complaint has been made against the batters for running on the pitch. While the umpire is correct to tell the batsmen off, Mark Richardson cheekily opines on air that if the batsmen themselves are ready to spoil the pitch, why interfere? This is anyway the last innings...

Faster ball on the pads, Raymon tucks it through fine leg but Colin de Grandhomme quickly gets to his left from backward square leg and dives to stop the ball. The batsmen abort the thought of a single.
Now he comes forward seeing the loop and drives the ball straight back to Santner.
Doesn't want to come forward, happy to play off the back foot. Blocks it towards short mid-wicket again.
Once again he is across the stumps to play that, defending it towards short mid-wicket.
Landed well outside off, Reifer gets across to defend but misses and is hit on the pads.
Full and outside off, Chase drives it through the covers, gets it past short extra cover but Jeet Raval covers good ground to his left from mid off and dives to stop the ball. Just a single.
RR is down the track again, de Grandhomme shortens the length on seeing that and squared him up. The ball goes off the outside edge to point.
Another bouncer, ducked under again.
A bouncer on middle and leg, Raymon ducks.
Now he comes way down the track to try and counter the swing and movement, pushing the ball to cover.
That came in a long way. Pitched well outside off, Reifer came forward to defend but was beaten by the prodigious inward movement.
Another man catching on the leg side moves to the slips.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Slower through the air, outside off, RC looks to drive but is beaten by the away turn.
On the leg stump, flicked towards deep mid-wicket for a run.
A bit of loop on this one, outside off, Roston drives this inside out towards wide mid off for a single.
Full and outside off, defended back to the bowler.
Arrowed on the pads, Chase is beaten by pace as he misses his flick, to get hit on the pads.
And again. The length is held back a touch but the line is still wide outside off, RR feels for it and is beaten.
This time a needless poke from Raymon. The ball was pretty wide outside off and could have been left alone but Reifer reached out to push, only to miss.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
A bouncer on middle, Reifer ducks.
Full and wide outside off, left alone.
The batsman works it down the leg side.

FOUR! Too wide and too full outside off, Chase leans, reaches out and drives the ball through the covers. The fielder puts in a desperate dive near the ropes but in vain. Chase moves to 43 now and so does this stand.
Ball hits the batsman low on the pads. One run added to the total. The umpire signals a leg bye.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.

A bit of a mix-up but safe in the end. Chase punches this towards point and there is a bit of miscommunication between the two batsmen for the single. Eventually they go for the run and make it. Direct hit at Santner's end could have had Chase.
Full and on the leg stump, defended with a lunge to the bowler.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
A surprising bouncer, but nowhere near the pace of Wagner, comfortably ducked by Reifer.
One more leave outside off.
Outside off, not played at.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off, pretty wide, left alone.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
Fuller on middle, defended back to the bowler.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Full and outside off, driven towards long off for a run.
Works this through the leg side for a single.
Full on middle, driven back to the bowler.
First bowl of the match for Santner. Interesting.
FOUR! Another outside edge! They just can't plug that gap! Outside off, now Reifer looks to drive, only to get an outside edge behind point to the fence.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Outside off, a play and a miss.
Wide outside off, left alone.
The batsman works it down the leg side. The batsmen have run through for a single.
FOUR! And a streaky shot to start the session. Full and outside off, Chase drives away from his body and gets a thick outside edge behind gully to third man!
The players are back out in the middle and the Kiwis get into a huddle.

Welcome back for the afternoon session. The Kiwis are a wicket away from getting into the tail. Just Roach, Cummins and Gabriel to come, who do not boast of the best of batting techniques. Not quite sure whether Ambris will bat again.
... DAY 4, SESSION 2 ... (FINAL ONE?)

The plans of batting through the day seem to be dashed for the Windies. Brathwaite would have been the ideal player to do that but he was the first one to be dismissed this morning. Majority of the batsmen have looked to play their shots and ended up gifting their wickets away. They look clueless against the short ball and the Black Caps will look to wrap this up by Tea. Join us back at 1340 LOCAL (0040 GMT)...

The Kiwis did not start well because they wasted the new ball. Boult was not happy with Southee as the latter was destroying the shape of the cherry by bowling cross-seam. But they still got wickets and the man ideal for this pitch, Neil Wagner, gave them more joy when he struck twice.

Everything which New Zealand would have wanted has happened in the morning session. Brathwaite was dismissed fairly cheaply and then, after a bit of a partnership, Hope and Dowrich got dismissed quickly in succession. Between those two, Ambris went off the ground retired hurt, after copping one on the arm from Wagner. He is currently in the hospital to have a precautionary x-ray.
Another full ball, flicked nicely wide of mid on. LUNCH ON DAY 4!
FOUR! Outstanding timing! Full again from Wagner, Reifer gets his bat down in time again and chips it uppishly over mid on for the second boundary of the over!
Expected response, a sharp bouncer, Raymon sways away.
FOUR! What a shot. Full on middle, Reifer times it straight, past mid on and gets a boundary!
A bouncer to test his footwork, Reifer gets out of the way.
A short ball, pulled through mid-wicket for a single.
Probably the last over before Lunch...
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Landed outside off, left alone again.
One more leave outside off.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Outside off, left alone,.
Full on middle, defended back to the bowler.
COLIN DE GRANDHOMME to bowl now.
Another nasty ball. This is around the face, Chase takes his eyes off it and only tries to fend it. The ball lobs off his arm to Ross Taylor at first slip. No appeal for a catch. Sportsmanship.
A short ball again, pulled towards Southee at mid-wicket.
The batsman gets up on his toes to play that one.
A short ball, Chase fends it just in front of short leg.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
A bouncer, pitched outside leg, Chase ducks to allow it over his head.
On a good length around off, defended from the crease.
A short ball at the rib cage, Raymon gets it down towards square leg.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
On a good length, gets steep bounce, Raymon fends it down.
Full and outside off, swinging in, Chase is looking to flick and mistimes it to mid-wicket. A single taken.
Around off, on a length, watchfully defended.
Full on middle, driven back to the bowler who has a shy back. The crowd likes the aggression from Wagner.
A bouncer now, ducked under.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Stays back on his crease and defends.
Outside off, left alone.
A short ball, pulled away through square leg for a single.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Landed outside off, a play and a miss from Raymon.

DROPPED! Well, he took a blinder in the first innings and in comparison, this was easier. Full and outside off, Reifer pushes hard and chips it back. Boult sticks out his right hand and then has to dive but the ball hits his right hand and is parried to cover.
A bouncer on middle, Reifer ducks.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Outside off, flayed through point for a single.
A bouncer around off, Raymon sways away.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Another short ball, pulled away for one more.
The batsman has stood up on his toes to play that one. They pick up a single. Gets off the mark.
A short delivery on middle, Chase pulls it towards square leg. Has to really hurry for the single.
Outside off, defended from the crease.
Outside off, a play and a miss.
Outside off, Reifer plays that inside the line, letting it through.
Landed outside off, left alone once again.
Outside off, driven through mid off for a single.
FOUR! Loose again. Full and wide outside off, Chase chases it again without moving his feet and gets a thick outside edge between the slips and gully to the third man fence.
Outside off, left alone.
A bouncer on middle, Raymon ducks.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
A short ball outside off, Reifer lets it through.
A short ball now, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.
A length ball down the leg side, Reifer hops to tuck it fine but the ball goes off his hips through square leg. A leg bye taken.
Slips this down the leg side, Reifer gets across and then tries to flick but misses.
On a good length on middle, Chase hops to defend.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
A short ball now, Chase sways away.
FOUR! BRILLIANT! Full and outside off, Chase leans into this one and drives it down the ground for a boundary. The shot of the day, in our opinion.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Outside off, fuller length to start, left alone.
TRENT BOULT is back on. Will he go for his stock ball - fuller length or bowl short stuff?
Another bouncer, Raymon gets out of the line.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
RAYMON REIFER walks in next, replacing Dowrich.

OUT! Well taken at short leg! As cool as a cucumber. Another one is bounced out. This is right on leg stump, gets extra bounce, Dowrich is two feet in the air as he tries to play it to the leg side but ends up playing it straight to Henry Nicholls at short leg. The fielder barely moves or reacts. Just takes it and then throws the ball away. Some swag. Windies are disintegrating now.
A short ball to greet the new man, Dowrich jumps to fend that to the off side. Thankfully, he is wearing an arm guard.
SHANE DOWRICH is the new man in, replacing Ambris.

Ambris is walking off. The moment he played that shot, he felt uncomfortable and started to walk towards the dressing room. The physio is out in the middle and has a long chat with him. Meanwhile, substitute Alzarri Joseph comes in with a few bats. Only he knows why. The physio tries convincing Ambris to battle it out but the youngster is adamant not to continue. Off he goes. Taylor pats him on his back.
A short ball on middle and leg, Ambris gets across and looks to pull but gets a bottom edge to short leg.
In line of the stumps, watchfully played out.
Outside off, slightly fuller, left alone.
A short ball, Ambris pulls it through mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman does well to stand tall and play that short delivery.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Another delay. The magic spray comes out. Ambris would be in pain but just do not understand why the Windies batsmen are not wearing elbow guards.

RAP! On the arm. Another batsman is hit. Wagner comes running in and bowls a sharp short ball around leg stump, Ambris ideally should be swaying or ducking or playing the pull or hook but he takes his eyes off the ball. Tries fending it with his eyes shut and wears it on the sweat band.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.

TOP EDGE, FOUR! Another boundary which has not looked the least bit convincing. Wagner bangs it in short, around off and Ambris swivels to pull. The ball is only 133.7 kph but Ambris is still beaten by pace and is late into the shot. He gets a thin top edge and then gets hit on the helmet. The ball then flies over the first slip fielder to the third man fence.
Another short ball, Chase swivels and pulls it through square leg for a single.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
EDGED, FOUR! Full and wide outside off, Roston chases it away from his body and gets a thick outside edge past point to the fence behind.
Another loose shot. Full and outside off, Roston looks to drive the ball through the covers but gets a thickish inside edge towards mid-wicket. A single taken.
That ball has taken the inside edge onto the pads.
Gets this fuller now, nice mix of length, makes it to swing as well. Chase flicks it loosely to mid-wicket.
On a length around off, watchfully defended from his crease.
Shorter in length, outside off, left alone.
A bouncer on middle, Chase ducks.
Sunil Ambris is the new man in.

OUT! The Windies are in dire straits now! Shattering apart without any kind of resistance. The short ball ploy works wonders for the Kiwis. This was coming after Wagner hit the batsman on the forearm but Hope instead of showing a circumspect approach goes for a pull cum hook shot. It is a well-directed bouncer as well, fast and accurate on middle and leg. Shoots off the deck, Hope is not in a good position as the ball gets big on him but he still commits to it. Ends up top edging his pull and the ball skies towards deep backward square leg. Colin de Grandhomme lines it up and pouches it safely. Wagner is absolutely pumped and vents out his aggression. The procession continues for the visitors.

Hope is getting some medical attention. He hasn't got an elbow guard in place, always a risky thing to do especially against a fast bowler who likes bowling short. Let's hope he is alright. Meanwhile, drinks has been taken.

Oh... that's nasty! Hope probably misread the length on this occasion. He was coming a touch forward but the ball is short and directed right at the body. Hope takes his eyes off the ball and takes a blow on his right forearm. Wagner gives him a long hard stare.
FOUR! Another good looking shot from Shai Hope. Half volley outside off, Hope strides ahead and times his drive to perfection. Gets it past the diving cover fielder for a boundary.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Shaping away on a good length, Shai plants his front foot across to allow it through.
Good delivery to begin with. Good length delivery on middle and off, swinging in. Hope accounts for the inward movement nicely and plays it with an angled bat to point.
Neil Wagner comes into the attack. Two slips and a gully in place.
Fractionally overpitched on off, eased past the bowler down the ground. Jeet Raval runs to his right and keeps it down to a single.
A short delivery, not that well-directed. Hope ducks under the bumper.
Full length ball attacking the stumps, played with soft hands to mid on.
Shaping in prodigiously, Chase clips it tentatively to square leg for a run.
Half volley wide outside off, Chase drives it brilliantly but finds the fielder at covers.

Ooh... that almost sneaked through! Fuller in length around off, swinging in substantially. Chase is late to get his bat down and somehow manages to keep it out off the inner half of the bat past the leg stump.
Bouncer, Hope is alert to it and ducks under it.

FOUR! Well played! Boult comes from around the wicket and bowls a short of a length ball around off. Hope hops back and guides it with an angled blade in the gap between third slip and gully and picks up another boundary.
Boult comes over the wicket and bowls a shortish delivery around off, Hope rises with the bounce and places it behind point for a well-earned couple of runs.
Back of a length ball around off, Hope makes good use of the depth of the crease and defends it to cover-point.
Leaving Hope after pitching, he plants his front foot across and lets it go.
Overpitched around off, driven crisply but straight to the man at deepish mid off.
Very full delivery around off, Roston jams it out back to the bowler.
Good looking shot! Full delivery, Chase shuffles across and clips it to deep mid-wicket for a couple.
FOUR! Elegant! That will give him confidence. Half volley outside off, Chase drives it through covers and the ball races to the fence.
Nice shape on that one, swinging away on a fullish length. Chase doesn't flirt with that.
Fractionally overpitched on off, Roston eases it past a crouching Southee to mid off.
Good length ball outside off, moving away. Chase points his bat skywards and lets it go.
Boult is walking off the field. Might be going back to take a breather.

FOUR! Textbook stuff! For all the youngsters out there, this is how you should drive a ball. Fullish delivery, angling into Hope. He puts a confident stride forward and caresses it through mid on from the full face of the bat. Away she whistles to the fence. Good followthrough of the bat after he played it, one for the cameramen to capture for the newspaper headlines.
Change of bat for Shai Hope.
Similar delivery, Hope shuffles across and taps it to mid-wicket.
Shaping in on a length, pushed back to Boult who mimes a throw back to the keeper.
Short ball well outside off, Shai pulls it to deepish mid-wicket.
Angling on a fullish length on off, Hope strides forward and drives it crisply to mid off.
This one is wide outside off, Hope doesn't go for an expansive stroke.
Sits deep in the crease and blocks this shortish delivery to block it.
Bouncer on off, pulled with command through square leg to rotate strike.
Third leave in a row, remains circumspect in approach.
Outside off, left alone.
Good length ball outside off, Hope makes an assured leave.
Back of a length delivery, defended solidly off the back foot.
Loose from Chase! Full length ball outside off, Roston goes for a booming drive but gets it off the outer half past point. A couple taken.
In the zone of apprehension, Chase lets it go.
Angling into Chase who tucks it to the leg side.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Fullish delivery outside off, driven to covers.
Roston Chase strides out to bat.

OUT! Gone! The big fish departs and probably with that, the hopes for the visitors fade away. 200th Test wicket for Trent Boult, 6th Kiwi bowler to achieve this landmark. A great achievement for him. He switches the angle and comes from around the wicket. Bowls a shortish delivery outside off, angling in. Brathwaite hops a touch and goes for the cut but a bit of extra bounce does him in. The ball flies off the outer half of the bat at a quick pace towards Williamson at gully. He is sharp as a hawk, crouches to his right and takes a brilliant catch. Falls down after taking it. New Zealand continue to rule the roost in home conditions and are 7 wickets shy of a win.

Scott Styris makes a good point on air. He doesn't doubt the talent that Shimron Hetmyer has but feels that he needs to be groomed in a better way. Australians usually slot newcomers at No. 5 or 6 which allows them to evaluate the conditions and adapt according to that.
Back of a length delivery, Hope hops and keeps it out.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
In the zone of apprehension, Hope doesn't fiddle with it.
Angling away on a good length, shouldered arms to.
A short delivery which has been pulled away. They pick up a single.
Boult has been officially warned for stepping on the danger area on his followthrough. He is a really key member for New Zealand. Needs to be careful.
Short ball, sits up nicely for Brathwaite. He pulls it with aplomb to deep square leg. Boult sprints to his left and does well to keep it to a brace.
A hat-trick of leaves to end the over.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
On a length outside off, left alone.
If he was a tad late in playing that one, he would have been a candidate for an LBW. Full delivery on off, swinging in late. Hope brings his bat down at an angle and flicks it to square leg.
False shot! On a drivable length, Hope goes for a booming drive but gets it off the inner half of the bat to mid on.
Angling away from Hope who plants his front foot across to allow it through.
Another bouncer, Brathwaite shuffles and help pulls it to short fine leg. Good over from Southee.
The batsman has stood up on his toes to play that one.
Trying to tuck up the batsman with a short one down the leg side, Kraigg moves inside the line and misses his tuck.
Southee comes around the wicket now. There is a deep mid-wicket in place. Short stuff to continue.
He is looking uncomfortable against the short stuff. Dances around in his crease and pulls it awkwardly towards short fine leg.

Ooh... lucky! On a length on off, Brathwaite hops and tries to help it across but seems to have got a bottom edge onto his pads. The ball lobs up as the short leg fielder tries to get to it. Fails to do so and the ball falls down on the track.
That was poor! You can't play like that to a short delivery. Southee hits the deck hard on off. Brathwaite shuffles across and lets it go. The ball just goes past his waist and over the stumps.
Full delivery in line of the stumps, pushed off the front foot to mid on.
Back of a length ball, slanting across Hope. He hops and keeps it out.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Hangs back to the good length delivery and blocks it with a straight bat.
There is a bit of issue with  the bottom half of Brathwaite's bat.
In the zone outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Elegant! Half volley outside off, Hope leans into it and punches it through extra cover for a majestic boundary. Didn't try to over hit that. Just timed it to perfection.
Trent Boult to bowl from the other end.
Fullish delivery attacking the stumps, patted to deepish mid on for a quick run. 6 from the first over of the day.
Short delivery on middle, comes at a nice height to Brathwaite. He swivels across and pulls it to deep backward square leg for a run.
This is good positive cricket from the Windies! Full length ball on off, Hope plays it with soft hands to mid on. Calls loud and clearly for a run and gets good response. Makes his crease with ease.
This one swings in on a fuller length, Brathwaite shuffles a touch and plays it to mid on for a run.
First runs of the day! Short and width on offer, Kraigg flashes it past point. Santner gives it a chase, slides near the fence and saves a couple of runs for his side.

On the money straightaway! Length delivery in the corridor of uncertainty, shaping away after pitching. Brathwaite gets opened up in his stance and gets a thick outside edge that falls short of second slip. Signs of things to come?

We are ready to get rolling. Kraigg Brathwaite and Shai Hope to continue their innings. A lot of hope lies on the shoulders of the current pair. It will be a testing first hour for them. Can they survive and flourish? Tim Southee to bowl first up this morning. Two slips, a gully and a short extra cover in place. Here we go...

The Kiwis are holding all the aces. Their new-ball bowlers, Trent Boult and Tim Southee are reveling bowling on a track which has quickened up. With 413 more runs to defend, the hosts are the favourites to take the series 2-0. Will things go according to plan? Or will an anti-climax occur? Welcome to the coverage of Day 4 which might be the final day itself.

The Windies do not need to look far for inspiration. After being pummeled into submission in Birmingham, Kraigg Brathwaite and Shai Hope scripted a fairy tale win for them in Headingley. Will that happen again? Chances are bleak considering the reckless approach of the visiting batsmen in this tour so far.

The sun is shining in all its glory in Hamilton as we gear up for another absorbing day of  Test cricket. Ironically, it is all gloomy for the visitors at the moment but these are situations which spark the possibility of emergence of heroes.
... DAY 4, MORNING SESSION ...

Earlier, a terrific ton from Taylor and handy contributions from Williamson and the lower order set the game up for them. The Windies bowlers tried their best but their batsmen are again threatening to undo all the hard work put in. Will sanity prevail and the visitors thrive under pressure? Or will it be a cakewalk for the home side? There is forecast for rain tomorrow but let's hope the weather holds up. Join us to catch all the action. Till then, cheers!

Hard to fathom the mindset from the visiting side. No real application being shown from the batsmen when the situation demands it. With still two days to go, it is an uphill task for the tourists to stage a fightback. Life is not easy for them as the New Zealand bowlers are breathing fire. A lot will depend on Kraigg Brathwaite if they are to get out of jail.

Taylor is happy with his knock and also with the situation his team is in. Informs that Martin Crowe wanted him to get past his landmark way back in 2006. Is happy that he finally got it today. On him trusting the lower order batsmen, Taylor says that he was not that worried as the team was in good shape anyways. Tears come in his eyes when asked about Martin Crowe and says that he would be definitely happy that Taylor has got his 17th Test ton.

New Zealand couldn't have asked for anything better. They head back to their dressing room with their heads held high. The Windies were already teetering, facing a mammoth target of 444 and to add insult to injury, they have lost two wickets in a jiffy. Boult continued his belligerent form while the birthday boy, Tim Southee is on song too as both of them have picked a wicket apiece.
In the channel outside off, Hope plants his front foot across and lets it go. THAT'S STUMPS ON DAY 3!
Tentative but Brathwaite will be happy that he survives! Fuller in length, swinging away. Brathwaite pokes at it tentatively and gets it off the outer half past the slip cordon. A single taken.
Boult comes from around the wicket and bowls a back of a length ball on off. Brathwaite hangs back and defends it stoutly.
Shaping away prodigiously, Kraigg hangs back and makes an assured leave.
Leg bye! Swinging down the leg side this time, Hope tries to play it across but gets hit on the pads. The ball rolls to the leg side and the batsmen sneak in a run.
Angling away on a length from Hope. He shuffles across and lets it go.
The last over of the day coming up.
Hope dances in his crease and somehow tucks it towards square leg for a run and will retain strike.
Full length ball attacking the stumps, patted to mid on.
Fullish delivery, swinging in, Hope strides forward and blocks it.
Shai Hope strides out to bat in his slotted position. Can he survive?

OUT! This is happening all too quickly for the visitors. The birthday boy gets a wicket. This was a nothing shot from the youngster though. Fractionally overpitched around off, Hetmyer goes for a booming drive with minimal feet movement and miscues his drive completely. Wagner at wide mid off gets low to his right and pouches it easily. Disappointing from the Windies, they are going down without a fight. New Zealand need 8 more wickets for a victory.
FOUR! Shot! Full length delivery, in the arc for Hetmyer. He leans forward and drives it nicely through mid on to find the fence.
Ooh... that inswing! Full length ball on middle, Hetmyer waits inside the crease gingerly and blocks it out besides the pitch on the leg side.
Another delivery in the same channel, Brathwaite hops and manages to keep it out.

Making the batsman hop. Shortish delivery on middle, it is pretty well-directed. Brathwaite is on his toes as he tries to block it but gets an inside edge down the track. The short leg is waiting for such a false stroke.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Angling away on a length. Brathwaite taps it to point with an open bat face.
Back of a length delivery in line of the stumps, Kraigg defends it with a straight bat.
Angling into Brathwaite who clips it through square leg. Wagner in the deep runs to his left and keeps it down to a couple.
Fuller in length outside off, shaping away. Hetmyer doesn't go for an expansive shot.
In the zone outside off, left alone.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! Confidence at its best! Short delivery in line of the stumps, sits up nicely for Hetmyer. He stands tall and nails the pull over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Angling into Hetmyer from around the wicket. He hangs deep in the crease and plays it with soft hands to mid on.
Back of a length delivery, shaping away, Brathwaite punches it through covers for a run.
On a length in line of the stumps, tucked to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Short of a length ball slanting across Kraigg. He hangs back and taps it to covers.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have run through for a single.
In the corridor of uncertainty, Shimron points his bat skywards to allow it through.
FOUR! Elegant! Half volley outside off, Hetmyer leans into it and caresses it through covers to find the fence.
Bangs in a short delivery, Hetmyer ducks under it nicely.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
FOUR! Brilliant! Sit back and applaud. Fullish delivery around off, Brathwaite shuffles a touch and drives it crisply through mid on for a delightful boundary.
Slips this one down the leg side, Brathwaite tries to clip it but misses.
Hangs back to the back of the length delivery and blocks it with a straight bat.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
He looks to take on the bowlers from the word go. On a drivable length around off, swinging away. Hetmyer drives it uppishly over the cover region for a couple and gets off the mark.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
That's a brute of a delivery! Good length ball in the zone of apprehension, straightens after pitching. Hetmyer feels for it and is beaten all ends up.
Shimron Hetmyer comes out to bat.

OUT! Yes, it is a fair catch. Wicket no. 199 for Trent Boult! He continues to flourish in home conditions. Good length delivery on middle and off, seams away after hitting the deck. Powell is caught in the crease and gets opened up in his stance. The line is such that he has to poke at it. Ends up getting a thick outside edge that flies towards third slip. Southee stationed there crouches to his left and seems to have taken it inches above the ground. The Black Caps start celebrating but the umpires tell them to hold on. They get together and decide to take the call upstairs. Is it a clean catch? The close in angle on the replay confirms that it indeed is. Sharp take from Southee. Powell has to go for a duck and he bags a pair. Ideal start for the hosts.
Kieran Powell has been caught in the slips but the umpires tell him to wait. They are checking whether Southee has taken the catch cleanly or not.
Length delivery around off, shaping away. Powell plants his front foot across and lets it go.

A peach of a delivery but just misses the hat-trick by an inch. Runs in and bowls a good length ball on middle, gets it to straighten after pitching. Powell is squared up and looks to defend it but gets hit on the thigh pad. A casual appeal follows but it is turned down. Height was the factor.
Trent Boult to share the new ball from the other end. Remember, he is on a hat-trick. Three slips and a gully waiting behind. Can he take it?
In the zone of apprehension, Brathwaite makes an assured leave.
Dug in short, Kraigg sits underneath it.
On a length outside off, shaping away. Brathwaite shoulders his arms to it.
FOUR! The Windies are away! On a length on middle and leg, Brathwaite moves inside the line and tickles it past the keeper to get off the mark with a boundary.
In the zone outside off, a bit of nibble in the air. Kraigg doesn't fiddle with it.
Bouncer in line of the stumps, Brathwaite ducks under it.
